title: Strong's Core Lexicon
note: This is the curated starter lexicon that ships inside the app - the words the Jeremiah study guide actually leans on, plus common vocabulary. Run tools/import_strongs.py to replace it with the complete Hebrew and Greek dictionaries and word-level tagging.

H3068.gloss: Yahweh, the self-existent One; the covenant name of God
H3068.def: From H1961 (to be, to become). Rendered LORD in most English versions and Yahweh in the World English Bible.

H430.def: Plural of H433, used of the true God with singular verbs - a plural of majesty rather than number.

H1697.def: From H1696 (to speak). In Hebrew a word is also an event: the same noun covers what is said and what is done about it.

H5002.def: Almost always in the formula 'declares Yahweh', marking the speech as directly quoted rather than reported.

H8451.def: From H3384 (to throw, to point out). The root sense is showing the way rather than issuing statutes.

H1285.def: Covenants are 'cut' (karath) rather than made, from the ceremony of dividing an animal and passing between the pieces.

H8245.gloss: to watch, to be alert, to be sleepless
H8245.def: Used in Jeremiah 1:12 - 'I watch over my word to perform it' - as a pun on H8247, the almond.
H8245.derivation: The almond is the shaqed because it is the shoqed - the watcher, the first tree to wake in late winter.

H8247.def: The earliest tree in the land to blossom, breaking dormancy while everything else is still asleep.

H1692.gloss: to cling, cleave, stick to, be joined
H1692.def: The verb of Genesis 2:24, where a man cleaves to his wife. Jeremiah 13:11 uses it of Israel clinging to Yahweh like a waistcloth to the body.

H232.def: The innermost garment worn against the skin, not an ornamental sash. The sign-act of Jeremiah 13 turns on the intimacy of the item.

H7725.gloss: to turn back, return, repent, restore
H7725.def: The single most important verb in Jeremiah, used more than a hundred times. Turning away and turning back are the same word, which is why the accusation and the invitation sound alike.

H1865.def: The technical term of the jubilee legislation. Jeremiah 34:17 turns it into a bitter pun: you would not proclaim deror to your brothers, so I proclaim deror to the sword.

H6780.def: Not a bough of a standing tree but the green shoot that comes up out of a cut stump - the messianic title of Jeremiah 23:5 and 33:15.

H1350.def: The participle go'el is the relative obliged to buy back a family member sold into slavery, redeem forfeited land, or stand up in court on their behalf. Jeremiah 50:34 - 'their Redeemer is strong'.

H4853.def: The double meaning drives Jeremiah 23:33-40, where the people sneer 'what is the burden of Yahweh?' and the phrase is confiscated from them.

H8414.def: With H922 it forms the phrase of Genesis 1:2, which Jeremiah 4:23 reuses to describe creation running backwards.

H922.def: Occurs only three times in the Hebrew Bible, always paired with H8414.

H4032.def: In the phrase magor missabib, 'terror on every side' - Jeremiah's signature expression, used to rename Pashhur in chapter 20 and later aimed at Egypt and the desert tribes.

H4726.def: Jeremiah 2:13 - the spring of living waters that was forsaken. A maqor supplies without being stored.

H953.def: A cistern is chiselled out of limestone and plastered by hand. The same word covers the pit Jeremiah was lowered into in chapter 38.

H2416.def: 'Living water' means moving water - a spring or stream rather than anything held in a tank.

H3335.def: The verb of the potter at his wheel in Jeremiah 18, and of God forming man from the dust in Genesis 2:7 and forming Jeremiah in the womb in 1:5.

H3627.def: Used of the temple vessels carried to Babylon and of the marred vessel remade on the wheel.

H2789.def: The fired clay flask of Jeremiah 19, broken at the Potsherd Gate, which cannot be remade once baked.

H5158.def: A wadi roars after winter rain and is dry in summer. Jeremiah 15:18 asks whether Yahweh has become 'as waters that fail' - a wadi to a thirsty traveller.

H3820.def: In Hebrew the heart is the seat of thought and decision more than of feeling. Jeremiah 17:9 and 31:33 both turn on it.

H5315.def: The whole living creature rather than an immaterial part of one. 'Your life as your spoil' is nephesh.

H7307.def: The same word covers the wind off the desert, the breath in a body, and the Spirit of God.

H2617.gloss: loving kindness, steadfast love, covenant faithfulness
H2617.def: Loyal love inside a committed relationship - the quality Jeremiah 9:24 says God delights in and 31:3 says drew Israel.

H7355.gloss: to have compassion, to love deeply
H7355.def: Built on the root for womb (H7358). The 'my heart yearns for him' of Jeremiah 31:20 is this word - visceral, parental compassion.

H5162.gloss: to be sorry, to relent, to comfort, to be moved to pity
H5162.def: The verb behind 'I relent of the disaster' in Jeremiah 18:8 and 'I grieve over the distress I have brought' in 42:10.

H6664.def: In Yahweh Tsidkenu, 'Yahweh our Righteousness' - the name given to the Branch in Jeremiah 23:6 and to Jerusalem in 33:16.

H4941.def: Doing mishpat is the standard the kings of Jeremiah 22 are audited by - and 22:16 calls doing it 'knowing me'.

H7965.def: Not merely the absence of war. Jeremiah 29:7 tells the exiles to seek the shalom of Babylon, and 6:14 condemns those who say shalom when there is none.

H571.def: From H539. Truth here is what holds weight when leaned on, not merely what corresponds to fact.

H8267.def: The word for the false prophets' message throughout Jeremiah - a lie that is preached rather than merely told.

H2451.def: One of the three boasts disqualified in Jeremiah 9:23, and the thing Edom is famous for and loses in 49:7.

H3045.gloss: to know, to perceive, to be acquainted with
H3045.def: Relational knowledge, not information. Jeremiah 24:7 promises a heart to yada Him, and 31:34 says all will yada Him.

H8085.gloss: to hear, to listen, to obey
H8085.def: Hearing and obeying are the same act in Hebrew. 'They have not listened' in Jeremiah always means more than that they failed to register the sound.

H2398.gloss: to sin, to miss the mark
H2398.def: The base term for offence against God or neighbour.

H5771.def: Crooked or twisted conduct, and by extension the guilt it incurs. Jeremiah 50:20 - the avon of Israel will be sought and not found.

H6588.def: The strongest of the three main sin words - a deliberate breach of relationship rather than a lapse.

H5545.def: Used only of God forgiving. Jeremiah 31:34 and 50:20 both use it.

H2734.gloss: to burn, to be kindled with anger
H2734.def: Anger described as heat rather than as noise.

H3372.gloss: to fear, to revere, to be afraid
H3372.def: Covers both terror and reverence; context decides which.

H157.def: Jeremiah 31:3 - 'I have loved you with an everlasting love' - places the loving before the drawing.

H5769.def: Time stretching out of sight in either direction. The 'everlasting love' and 'everlasting covenant' of Jeremiah both use it.

H5030.def: One who speaks for another. Jeremiah 23 tests the office by whether the man has stood in Yahweh's council.

H3548.def: Jeremiah was born into a priestly family at Anathoth.

H4428.def: Five kings of Judah reigned during Jeremiah's ministry.

H7462.gloss: to pasture, to tend, to shepherd
H7462.def: The participle ro'eh is a shepherd, used throughout Jeremiah for Judah's leaders - who are indicted in chapter 23 for scattering the flock.

H6629.def: Jeremiah 50:6 - 'my people have been lost sheep'.

H7611.def: The thread running through the whole book: judgement is never total, and a she'erith survives it.

H894.def: Written as the cipher Sheshach in Jeremiah 25:26 and 51:41, with the letters of the alphabet reversed.

H4714.def: The place Judah is repeatedly forbidden to return to, and where the surviving remnant ends up in chapters 43 and 44.

H6726.def: The temple hill, and by extension Jerusalem and its people.

H3389.def: Named more than a hundred times in Jeremiah.

H3063.def: The southern kingdom, and the tribe from which the Branch comes.

H3478.gloss: Israel, one who strives with God
H3478.def: In Jeremiah usually the northern kingdom, already deported, and repeatedly invited home in chapter 3.

H3645.gloss: Chemosh, the national god of Moab
H3645.def: Jeremiah 48:7 has him going into exile with his own priests and princes.

H4445.gloss: Milcom, the national god of Ammon
H4445.def: Jeremiah 49:3 sends him into captivity as it does Chemosh.

G3056.def: The Greek counterpart to the Hebrew dabar, carrying both what is said and the reasoning behind it.

G4487.def: A particular utterance rather than the whole message.

G1242.def: The Greek rendering of berit, and the word behind 'New Testament'. Hebrews quotes Jeremiah 31:31-34 twice using it.

G2537.def: New in quality rather than merely new in time - the adjective in 'new covenant'.

G26.def: Committed love directed at another's good; the New Testament's usual counterpart to chesed.

G1656.def: The Septuagint's regular translation of chesed.

G863.gloss: to send away, release, forgive, leave
G863.def: The verb behind 'forgive' in the Gospels - literally to let go of something.

G1343.def: The Greek counterpart to tsedeq, and the term behind Paul's account of a righteousness credited rather than achieved.

G4102.def: Both the trusting and the trustworthiness, as with the Hebrew emunah.

G1680.def: Confident expectation rather than wishing. Jeremiah 29:11 promises a future and an elpis in the Septuagint tradition.

G1515.def: The Septuagint's standard rendering of shalom.

G4991.def: Deliverance out of a danger, not only forgiveness of sin.

G3341.def: The New Testament's nearest term to shuv, though it emphasises the turn of mind where the Hebrew emphasises the turn of direction.

G2588.def: The counterpart to leb - the seat of thought and decision.

G4151.def: The counterpart to ruach, carrying the same triple sense.

G2962.def: The Septuagint uses it where the Hebrew has the divine name, which is why English Bibles print LORD.

G4166.def: John 10 and Hebrews 13:20 answer Jeremiah 23 with a shepherd who does not scatter the flock.

G4263.def: 'Sheep without a shepherd' in Matthew 9:36 echoes Jeremiah 50:6.

G3005.gloss: a remnant, what is left over
G3005.def: Romans 11:5 - 'a remnant according to the election of grace', the New Testament's continuation of she'erith.

G2419.def: The transliterated Hebrew form, used alongside the Hellenised Hierosoluma.

G897.def: Revelation 17 and 18 reuse Jeremiah 50-51 almost phrase for phrase, including 'come out of her, my people'.
